strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis of spatial acceleration artifacts in DiTs with clear visualizations demonstrating aliasing, distribution mismatch, and noise-timestep misalignment issues
Training-free methodology providing immediate applicability to existing pre-trained models without retraining requirements
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (FLUX-1-dev, SD3), acceleration factors (2-7×), and diverse metrics (ImageReward, CLIP-IQA, NIQUE, T2I-CompBench, GenEval)
Strong empirical results achieving 5.33× and 7.0× speedups with superior image quality and substantially lower artifact ratios compared to baselines
Thorough ablation studies systematically isolating contributions of NT-Matching, edge region selection, and upsampling methods
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and precise mathematical formulation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques (mixed-resolution interpolation, standard distribution matching, conventional edge detection) without fundamental new concepts

Architecture-specific design tailored exclusively to flow-matching DiTs; no evaluation on epsilon-prediction, score-based, or other DiT variants; applicability to diffusion UNets or other architectures unclear

Weak theoretical justification for why mixed-resolution upsampling specifically addresses identified problems; assumptions in Eqs. 8-10 about latent distributions may not universally hold; optimal three-stage decomposition not theoretically motivated

Critical implementation details underspecified: edge detection method choice (VAE vs gradient kernel) insufficiently justified, noise/timestep matching optimization procedure vaguely described as 'numerical search', stage-wise parameter computation (Eq. 7) inadequately documented
Narrow evaluation scope: only 1024×1024 images tested; no assessment on other resolutions, aspect ratios, video, 3D, or other DiT applications; no user studies on quality-speedup tradeoffs
Computational overhead of components undercharacterized in Table S2; edge detection robustness not analyzed; no discussion of failure modes or sensitivity to image content
Limited ablations on edge detection strategies; visual comparisons in Fig. 6 appear cherry-picked rather than systematic; missing comparisons with some recent spatial acceleration methods

Methodological concerns: block-diagonal covariance assumption in Eq. 5 needs justification; fixed upsampling ratio choices appear empirically driven; adaptive ratio shows minimal gains despite added complexity

strengths: Well-motivated identification of concrete artifacts (aliasing and mismatch) in spatial acceleration with clear visualization and targeted solutions for each
Training-free approach that works with pre-trained models (FLUX, SD3) without requiring retraining, making it immediately practical
Strong and consistent experimental results: 7.0× speedup on FLUX and 3.0× on SD3 with minimal quality degradation across diverse evaluation metrics

Comprehensive evaluation: multiple models, speedup levels, multiple quality metrics (FID, NIQE, CLIP-IQA), text-alignment metrics (T2I-CompBench, GenEval), ablation studies, and extensive uncurated qualitative results
Demonstrates complementarity with caching methods: achieves 7.94× speedup when combined with temporal acceleration on FLUX 7×
Technically sound mathematical framework based on flow matching theory with correct derivations for noise injection and NT-DM
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of artifacts, method stages, and comparative results across baselines
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: three-stage resolution strategy is standard in cascaded diffusion models; noise injection formula (Eq. 6) is acknowledged as inspired by prior work [21]; main novel component (NT-DM) relies on heuristic numerical optimization rather than principled derivation

Restricted applicability: NT-DM is specifically tailored to flow-matching models; effectiveness on score-based or DDIM-style diffusion is unverified; only evaluated on text-to-image; generalization to video, audio, or 3D unexplored

Design choices lack sufficient justification: (1) Why Canny edge detection over alternatives? No comparison with other edge detectors. (2) Top-k patch selection is purely empirical with no principled selection criterion. (3) Three-stage design not systematically justified—why not 2, 4, or 5 stages?

NT-DM is ad-hoc: optimization via 'numerical search' details are vague; solution Σ'=I-cΣ motivated only by 'symmetry'; empirically determined {h_k}, c values vary significantly across configurations (Table S1), suggesting limited generalization

Incomplete baseline comparisons: (1) Bottleneck Sampling is concurrent work (arxiv:2503.18940, 2025)—fairness unclear. (2) ToCa performance is suspiciously poor; proper tuning uncertain. (3) Missing comparison with naive early upsampling. (4) RAS comparison missing on FLUX

Limited theoretical analysis: aliasing at edges is explained intuitively but not rigorously justified; relationship between timestep distribution deviation and artifact severity not quantified; no failure mode analysis or discussion of when method breaks

Reproducibility concerns: optimization procedure for {h_k}, c only described as 'numerical search' without details; k selection appears purely empirical; code availability not mentioned; VAE decoder overhead varies significantly (0.08% vs 0.71%) without explanation
VAE decoder overhead claim of 'negligible' is overstated for SD3 (0.71% of FLOPs); using VAE estimates for edge detection introduces potential error accumulation not discussed
